ratings.label: offense
ratings.description: How much damage you deal and how reliably you take enemies down.

ratings.label: defense
ratings.description: How hard you are to take down, through hit points, armor, dodging or other means.

ratings.label: support
ratings.description: How much you help allies succeed: healing, buffs, debuffs and battlefield control.

ratings.label: utility
ratings.description: How well you handle problems outside combat, when a fireball or an axe is not the answer.

ratings.label: difficulty
ratings.description: How much system knowledge you need to play the class well.

groups.label: High magic ability
groups.description: Full spellcasters with spell slots of every rank.

groups.label: Moderate magic ability
groups.description: Magic is central but narrower: fewer slots, or magical class powers instead of spells.

groups.label: Low magic ability
groups.description: Martial classes with a touch of magic, mostly optional focus spells.

groups.label: No magic ability
groups.description: Classes that rely on weapons, skills, gear and alchemy.

castingTypes.label: Prepared
castingTypes.description: Choose which spell goes into each slot at the start of the day, then cast those spells.

castingTypes.label: Spontaneous
castingTypes.description: Know a smaller repertoire of spells and cast any of them with any open slot of the right rank.

castingTypes.label: Prepared & spontaneous
castingTypes.description: Prepare most spells each morning, and cast a second set freely from a small repertoire.

statuses.label: Playtest
statuses.description: Public playtest; rules may change before print.

legend.howToUse: A character's class sets many of their core abilities, but there is plenty of room to specialize. These ratings are rough, opinionated estimates of how an average member of each class performs; subclasses, feats and party makeup can change things a lot.
legend.choice: Some classes make one fundamental choice, such as a cleric's doctrine or a sorcerer's bloodline, that swings their numbers a long way. Hatched squares show the range between the two extremes.
